title: Work That Splinters Into Tickets
eyebrow: Landed. The two-path rule is live and enforced

actions.fyi: Done and live for every session from its next turn. The reader signed the change with no findings. Override any decision below if one reads wrong.

content.label: What you saw
content.lead: One job in, five tickets out.

items: An agent sent to fix one thing meets the faults next to it — the same cause in five places, or five small breaks its one change would sweep up anyway.
Instead of fixing them while standing there, it files each as a new ticket and hands them out.
Each ticket then pays for a whole job: its own copy of the code, its own review, its own merge — for an edit that was already under the agent's hands.

content.label: Why it happens
content.lead: The rule that stops things evaporating has no edge, so everything falls the same side of it.

rows.title: The standing rule is loud and one-sided
rows.note: Every agent opens with: anything you notice outside the current job becomes a ticket, no exceptions, and a check enforces it. Filing is the only named path for a discovery.

rows.title: Nothing says what is inside the job
rows.note: No rule anywhere draws the line between a fault that belongs to the fix in hand and one that is genuinely separate. An agent takes the safe path the rule names: file a ticket.

rows.title: The in-job path exists and is never pointed at discoveries
rows.note: A job can already grow its own work items and fix them in the same tree, landing together. The rules mention it only as structure, never as where a related fault should go.

rows.title: The checks only push one way
rows.note: An unfiled find is punished. A needless ticket costs nothing — so five tickets is always the safe play, and the board fills with splinters.

content.label: The fix, as you ruled it
content.lead: Two recorded paths and no third way, held by the same check that ends every turn.

items: A related fault is added as a step of the current ticket and fixed there and then.
A separate thing gets its own ticket.
A fault that lives only in the session's memory is refused: the check that ends every turn blocks until it is recorded one of the two ways, and its refusal now names both.

blocks.label: Little new machinery
blocks.text: Both recording paths already exist; the work is the boundary in the standing rules, a wider net of phrases the check catches, and a refusal that names both paths.

decisions.title: Your complaint became a card the same turn
decisions.why: The rule that nothing noticed may evaporate applies to itself. It is cor-mq0g, promoted into the job this page follows.

decisions.title: Diagnosis only, until your ruling
decisions.why: Your standing instruction: a pointed-out problem gets a diagnosis, then waits for your go-ahead.

decisions.title: Two recorded paths, hard enforced
decisions.why: Your ruling. Related fault: a step of the current ticket, fixed there. Separate thing: its own ticket. A fault kept only in a session's memory is refused at the end of the turn.

decisions.title: The check stays a phrase net, but a much wider one
decisions.why: The turn's last words are the only thing the check can read, so it catches the phrasings that report an unrecorded fault. The net grows from a handful of phrases to the common ways of saying it, and each side of the rule gets a test that goes red if the net is weakened.

next.if_nothing: Nothing — the rule is live. Every session opens on the two-path rule, the end-of-turn check blocks a fault recorded neither way and names both, and the tests go red if anyone weakens it.

steps.step: Watch whether agents now grow their job instead of splintering it, and tighten the phrase net if a new wording slips through
